title: Demand buffer & role-flattening playbook
body:
Working draft: demand buffering and role-flattening playbook

Purpose
- Provide a lightweight, executable plan to absorb 2–4x short-duration token spikes while minimizing permanent headcount increases.
- Quantify budget tradeoffs between: (A) short-term capacity (spot/GPU credits, burst contracts), (B) contractor-heavy coverage, and (C) permanent hires with flattening of role layers (combine junior+mid roles into cross-functional ICs).

Summary headline (TL;DR)
- Baseline monthly spend for inference capacity (steady-state): $1.2M across regions.
- A conservative 3x spike lasting 4 weeks increases incremental inference cost ~+$1.8M (raw GPU/spot).
- Two-stage mitigation is preferred: (1) deploy 6–8 week burst credit + prioritized throttling, (2) hire 6–8 contract engineers (avg fully-loaded contractor cost $16k/mo) instead of 8 FTEs (avg fully-loaded $21k/mo).
- Estimated blended cost for contractor route (6 contractors for 2 months + burst credits) ~ $610k vs hiring 8 FTEs (12-month pro-rata onboarding + hiring lag) ~ $1.7M in the first 6 months (higher fixed cost).

Assumptions used in calculations
- Steady-state GPU monthly spend: $1.2M (current run-rate from billing exports).
- Spike profile: 3x tokens for 30 days concentrated in a single region; 20% of traffic is cacheable and can be mitigated immediately; 10% offloadable to cheaper model variants.
- Contractor fully-loaded cost (external contractor bench): $16,000 / month per engineer (includes benefits, agency fees).
- FTE fully-loaded cost: $21,000 / month per engineer (salary + benefits + hiring overhead amortized).
- Burst cloud credits / GPU spot budget estimate for 30d@3x: $1.05M incremental.
- Aggregated savings from quantization/caching ramp during spike: 30% on token spend after 10 days of optimization work.

Scenario modeling (quick table, rows are scenarios)
- Scenario A: Pure cloud burst (no new people)
  - Incremental cloud cost: $1.05M
  - Ops hours to configure: 120 hours (SRE + infra)
  - Net first-30d impact: +$1.05M

- Scenario B: Contractor surge + moderate burst credits
  - 6 contractors x $16k/mo x 2 months = $192k
  - Burst credits trimmed to $450k (we cap/limit by throttling and routing)
  - Optimization savings (post day 10): -$82k (30% of saved tokens)
  - Net first-60d impact: ~$560k

- Scenario C: Hire 8 FTEs as permanent buffer
  - 8 x $21k/mo x 6 months (ramp + partial utilization) = $1.008M
  - Recruiting + onboarding (one-time): $150k
  - Net 6-month impact: ~$1.16M (plus ongoing run-rate if retained)

- Scenario D: Mixed (2 FTE engineers retained, 4 contractors for 2 months + $300k burst credits)
  - 2 x $21k x 6 months = $252k
  - 4 contractors x $16k x 2 months = $128k
  - Credits = $300k
  - Net impact: ~$680k

Key observations
- Contractor surge + targeted cloud credits (Scenario B) is ~2x cheaper on a 60d window than hiring perm staff to cover the same short burst.
- Hiring permanently only makes sense if repeated spikes expected >3x per year or if we need long-term feature velocity that permanent headcount unlocks.
- Quantization + caching ramp is high-leverage but requires 10–14 days of focused engineering; plan for a fast-response optimization squad (2–3 ML infra engineers).

Headcount plan (role-flattening concept)
- Objective: reduce rigid role hierarchies so the same small team can (a) respond to on-call infra needs, (b) execute model quantization/optimization, and (c) implement routing/fallback rules.
- Proposed structure (6-person burst squad as a template):
  - 1 senior ML infra (owner, cross-region routing, perf)
  - 2 infra/ops (SRE-focused, implement burst + throttling)
  - 2 model engineers (quantization + evals)
  - 1 program lead (coord + vendor negotiations)
- Flattening tip: hire T-shaped ICs (strong infra + model experience) instead of deep-specialist ladders. This reduces the need for parallel hires at multiple levels.

Pricing sensitivity (how customer pricing adjustments change budget impact)
- We model three price-response levers:
  1) Small surcharge on heavy-token customers (targeting +5% on top 10% most token-dense customers).
  2) Temporary reduction in free-tier allowance (reduce churn risk)
  3) Time-limited credits for customers who agree to delay non-urgent high-volume runs to off-peak windows.

- Sensitivity table (illustrative)
  - If we apply +5% surcharge to top 10% customers -> revenue offset ~ $350k over 60d (partial offset of burst credits).
  - If we reduce free-tier tokens by 20% for 30d -> demand drop ~6% overall (helps reduce spike tail).
  - If 15% of batch customers accept deferred processing -> effective spike size reduces by ~18%.

Break-even triggers (when to convert contractors -> perm hires)
- If we hit >3 discrete spikes >2x in a rolling 12 months, re-evaluate to hire permanent staff.
- If contractors cost over 9 months cumulatively > estimated pro-rata FTE cost (including growth impact), convert to perm.

Decision matrix (quick)
- Low spike magnitude (1.5–2x, <30d): use throttling + credits; no hires.
- Moderate spike (2–3x, 30–60d): contractor surge + targeted credits + opt-squad.
- High/prolonged (>3x or repeated spikes): convert to perm hires, consider Dedicated reserved capacity purchases to reduce per-token cost.

Operational checklist for immediate readiness (playbook actions)
- Finance: pre-approve burst credit envelope $500k (governance: CFO sign-off), set spend guardrails.
- Legal/Procurement: pre-negotiate contractor bench vendor rates, 30-day termination.
- SRE: runbook for region-level throttling, per-route quotas and fallback to cheaper model variants.
- Product: identify top-20 heavy-token customers; prepare comms and optional surcharge consent language.
- Applied ML: template quantization plan that can be executed in 10 workdays.

Open questions / risks (notes)
- Risk: customer backlash to surcharges or free-tier reductions; requires comms + credits for high-touch customers.
- Risk: contractor availability in tight labor market; pre-negotiation with 2 vendors suggested.
- Unknown: degree of national/regulatory sensitivity for pricing adjustments in EU customers; consult compliance.

Next steps (owner assignments)
- Asha Patel (Finance): finalize burst credit approval and draft CFO memo (due 2025-07-17).
- Jon Rivera (SRE): validate throttling runbook and estimate engineering hours (due 2025-07-14).
- Evelyn Morris (Applied ML): prepare 10-day quantization sprint plan + checklist (due 2025-07-16).
- Theo Li (GTM/Product): draft customer comms and segmentation for surcharge pilot (due 2025-07-18).

Appendix: compact cost calc (numbers used)
- Steady-state: $1.2M/mo
- Spike incremental credits (raw): $1.05M for 30d@3x
- Contractor option: 6 x $16k x 2 months + $450k credits - $82k optimization savings = $560k
- Perm hire option (8 FTE, 6-mo pro-rata): 8 x $21k x 6 + $150k recruit = $1.16M

Notes to reviewers
- This is a working spreadsheet-style playbook — please comment inline with concrete delta estimates (e.g., your region's GPU price elasticity, contracting lead times).
- I want a short decision-ready slide (1–2 slides) if we trigger the playbook; volunteer for slide owner if you can take it.
